bibl.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: The result is a new global logbilinear regression model that combines the advantages of the two major model families in the literature: global matrix factorization and local context window methods.

span.label: word vector representations from co-occurrence statistics
span.quote: The statistics of word occurrences in a corpus is the primary source of information available to all unsupervised methods for learning word representations, and although many such methods now exist, the question still remains as to how meaning is generated from these statistics, and how the resulting word vectors might represent that meaning.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We propose a specific weighted least squares model that trains on global word-word co-occurrence counts and thus makes efficient use of statistics.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: learn word vectors from the global co-occurrence matrix via a log-bilinear model on ratios of co-occurrence probabilities, so vector differences encode meaning
span.quote: word vector learning should be with ratios of co-occurrence probabilities rather than the probabilities themselves

span.label: the origin of the linguistic regularities captured by word-vector arithmetic was not understood
span.note: what this limits: the explanatory claim about vector arithmetic: THE ORIGIN OF THESE REGULARITIES HAS REMAINED OPAQUE
span.quote: the origin of these regularities has remained opaque

span.label: The chosen exponent in the weighting function is justified only empirically, not derived.
span.note: what this limits: every result produced with the weighting function: WE OFFER ONLY EMPIRICAL MOTIVATION FOR CHOOSING THE VALUE 3/4 - the exponent is fitted, not derived
span.quote: Although we offer only empirical motivation for choosing the value 3/4, it is interesting that a similar fractional power scaling was found to give the best performance in (Mikolov et al., 2013a).

span.label: The head-to-head comparison with word2vec is confounded by many performance-affecting parameters.
span.note: what this limits: the head-to-head comparison with word2vec: A RIGOROUS QUANTITATIVE COMPARISON ... IS COMPLICATED BY THE EXISTENCE OF MANY PARAMETERS THAT HAVE A STRONG EFFECT ON PERFORMANCE
span.quote: A rigorous quantitative comparison of GloVe with word2vec is complicated by the existence of many parameters that have a strong effect on performance.

span.label: Unspecified parameters were left at defaults, a simplification the authors say a more thorough analysis should relax.
span.note: what this limits: every reported comparison, and it is the confound item 2 names: WE SET ANY UNSPECIFIED PARAMETERS TO THEIR DEFAULT VALUES, ASSUMING THAT THEY ARE CLOSE TO OPTIMAL, THOUGH WE ACKNOWLEDGE THAT THIS SIMPLIFICATION SHO[uld be noted]
span.quote: We set any unspecified parameters to their default values, assuming that they are close to optimal, though we acknowledge that this simplification should be relaxed in a more thorough analysis.

span.label: The largest-corpus (840B token) run used a different preprocessing, so its results are not comparable with the reported ones.
span.note: what this limits: the scalability demonstration specifically: TO DEMONSTRATE THE SCALABILITY OF THE MODEL, WE ALSO TRAINED IT ON A MUCH LARGER SIXTH CORPUS, CONTAINING 840 BILLION TOKENS OF WEB DATA, BUT IN THIS [case the conditions differ]
span.quote: To demonstrate the scalability of the model, we also trained it on a much larger sixth corpus, containing 840 billion tokens of web data, but in this case we did not lowercase the vocabulary, so the results are not directly comparable.

span.label: The comparison that establishes the headline result runs the competing method at default settings, assumed near-optimal, and the paper says the assumption should be relaxed.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that this model outperforms word2vec: unspecified parameters of the compared systems were left at default values on the assumption they are close to optimal, which the authors call a simplification that a more thorough analysis should relax
span.quote: We set any unspecified parameters to their default values, assuming that they are close to optimal, though we acknowledge that this simplification should be relaxed in a more thorough analysis

span.label: The exponent that shapes the weighting function has empirical motivation only.
span.note: what this limits: results that depend on the weighting function: the authors state they offer only empirical motivation for the value 3/4, noting a similar fractional power scaling was found elsewhere
span.quote: Although we offer only empirical motivation for choosing the value 3/4, it is interesting that a similar fractional power scaling was found to give the best performance

span.label: The distinction the model is built on is declared arbitrary by the authors.
span.note: what this limits: any interpretation of the two vector sets as different kinds of thing: the paper states the distinction between a word and a context word is arbitrary and that the two roles may be exchanged
span.quote: note that for word-word co-occurrence matrices, the distinction between a word and a context word is arbitrary and that we are free to exchange the two roles

span.label: The largest corpus in the paper was processed differently, so its numbers do not sit on the same scale as the rest.
span.note: what this limits: a comparison across the corpora reported here: for the 840-billion-token web corpus the vocabulary was not lowercased, and the authors state the results are therefore not directly comparable
span.quote: we also trained it on a much larger sixth corpus, containing 840 billion tokens of web data, but in this case we did not lowercase the vocabulary, so the results are not directly comparable

span.label: The complexity result rests on an assumed distribution rather than a measured one.
span.note: what this limits: the claim about how the model's cost scales: it requires assuming the number of co-occurrences of two words can be modelled as a power-law function of that pair's frequency rank
span.quote: In order to make any concrete statements about the number of nonzero elements in X, it is necessary to make some assumptions about the distribution of word co-occurrences. In particular, we will assume that the number of co-occurrences of word i with word j, Xi j , can be modeled as a power-law function of the frequency rank of that word pair

span.label: global matrix factorization (from latent semantic analysis) combined with local context windows to learn word vectors
span.quote: combines the advantages of the two major model families in the literature: global matrix factorization and local context window methods

span.label: word vector
span.quote: where w ∈ Rd are word vectors and ˜w ∈ Rd are separate context word vectors whose role will be discussed

span.label: context word
span.quote: the distinction between a word and a context word is arbitrary

span.label: word analogy
span.quote: introduced a new evaluation scheme based on word analogies that probes the finer structure of the word vector space

span.label: context window
span.quote: A context window that extends to the left and right of a target word will be called symmetric

span.label: syntactic subtask
span.quote: Performance is better on the syntactic subtask for small and asymmetric context windows

span.label: what the paper calls its own object - WORD VECTORS AND WORD REPRESENTATIONS, NEVER EMBEDDINGS: it uses those two terms 24 and 11 times; 'word embeddings' appears exactly once and describes another group's method rather than this paper's output, and 'distributional semantics' does not appear at all
span.quote: The result, GloVe, is a new global log-bilinear regression model for the unsupervised learning of word representations that outperforms other models on word analogy, word similarity, and named entity recognition tasks

span.label: 'word embeddings' IN THIS PAPER - SOMEONE ELSE'S OBJECT: the single occurrence attributes the term to Levy et al., alongside vLBL and ivLBL, as a rival PPMI-based approach; the authors never apply the word to what they themselves produce
span.quote: proposed closely-related vector log-bilinear models, vLBL and ivLBL, and Levy et al. (2014) proposed explicit word embeddings based on a PPMI metric

span.label: the analogy evaluation - AS DIMENSIONS OF DIFFERENCE, NOT DISTANCE: it probes the vector space by examining the various dimensions of difference between vectors rather than the scalar distance between them, which is why a model can win on similarity and lose on analogy
span.quote: introduced a new evaluation scheme based on word analogies that probes the finer structure of the word vector space by examining not the scalar distance between word vectors, but rather their various dimensions of difference

span.label: the context window - SYMMETRIC OR ASYMMETRIC, AND THE CHOICE MOVES ONE SUBTASK ONLY: a window extending both ways is called symmetric and one extending only left asymmetric, and the syntactic subtask specifically improves with small asymmetric windows
span.quote: A context window that extends to the left and right of a target word will be called symmetric, and one which extends only to the left will be called asymmetric

span.label: builds-on → global matrix factorization (LSA) and local context-window methods
span.quote: combines the advantages of the two major model families in the literature: global matrix factorization and local context

span.label: contradicts → Baroni et al. (2014)
span.quote: Currently, prediction-based models garner substantial support; for example, Baroni et al. (2014) argue that these models perform better across a range of tasks. In this work we argue that the two classes of methods are not dramatically different at a fundamental level since they both probe the underlying co-occurrence statistics of the corpus, but the efficiency with which the count-based methods capture global statistics can be advantageous.

span.label: extends → skip-gram and ivLBL window-based models
span.quote: Therefore, in this subsection we show how these models are related to our proposed model, as defined in Eqn. (8).

span.label: word vector —same-as→ context word
span.note: holds when: only when the co-occurrence matrix is symmetric · differs in: the random initialization of the two vector sets · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: When X is symmetric, W and ˜W are equivalent and differ only as a result of their random initializations; the two sets of vectors should perform equivalently

span.label: context window —causes→ syntactic subtask
span.quote: Performance is better on the syntactic subtask for small and asymmetric context windows, which aligns with the intuition that syntactic information is mostly drawn from the immediate context and can depend strongly on word order

span.label: 75% — accuracy on the word analogy task (GloVe headline result)
span.quote: its performance of 75% on a recent word analogy task

span.label: 6 billion — corpus size used to build the co-occurrence statistics
span.quote: from a 6 billion token corpus

span.label: GloVe, a global log-bilinear regression model trained on nonzero word-word co-occurrence counts, yields word vectors with meaningful linear substructure and 75% on word analogies, outperforming prior models on similarity and NER.
span.quote: The result is a new global logbilinear regression model that combines the advantages of the two major model families in the literature: global matrix factorization and local context window methods.

span.label: Meaning is encoded in RATIOS of co-occurrence probabilities, not raw counts — the ratio cancels noise from non-discriminative words.
span.quote: Only in the ratio does noise from non-discriminative words like water and fashion cancel out

span.label: word-word co-occurrence counts
span.quote: training only on the nonzero elements in a word-word cooccurrence matrix

span.label: word analogy accuracy
span.quote: its performance of 75% on a recent word analogy task

span.label: GloVe (Global Vectors)
span.quote: a new global logbilinear regression model that combines the advantages of the two major model families in the literature: global matrix factorization and local context window methods

span.label: word analogy task
span.quote: the analogy “king is to queen as man is to woman” should be encoded in the vector

span.label: correlation
span.quote: We compute Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient between this score and the human judgments.

span.label: regression
span.quote: The result is a new global logbilinear regression model that combines the advantages of the two major model families in the literature: global matrix factorization and local context window methods.
